items.title: Section: Refusing to Accept Another's Genuine Apology

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，他所侵犯，彼還如法平等悔謝。懷嫌恨心，欲損惱彼，不受其謝，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。雖復於彼無嫌恨心，不欲損惱，然由稟性不能堪忍，故不受謝，亦名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, having been wronged by another, are offered a sincere and proper apology in return, yet refuse to accept it out of a lingering resentment and a wish to keep hurting the other person, commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. Even where the bodhisattva harbours no actual resentment and has no wish to hurt the other person, but simply cannot, by native temperament, let the matter go, and so still refuses the apology — this too constitutes a violation and a transgression, and, according to the Taishō text, remains a tainted violation.

items.zh: 無違犯者，若欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說一切如前應知；若不如法、不平等謝；不受彼謝，亦無違犯。

items.title: Section: Harbouring a Grudge — And Master Cháng Bǎi on Learning to Let Go

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，於他懷忿，相續堅持，生已不捨，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。無違犯者，為斷彼故生起樂欲，廣說如前。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who harbour anger towards another being, holding it fast and continuing to nurse it, never releasing it once it has arisen — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. ... There is no violation for one who genuinely wishes to eliminate the grudge and works diligently towards doing so, as described earlier.

items.title: Section: Craving to Be Served by Disciples — the Buddha's Three Kinds of Students and Cunda's Final Offering — Patience-Progression Closes

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，貪著供事增上力故，以愛染心管御徒眾，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。無違犯者，不貪供侍，無愛染心管御徒眾。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, driven by the intensifying force of craving to be served and attended to, govern their following with a mind of attached, craving affection — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. ... There is no violation for one who does not crave being served or attended to, and governs the community without any mind of attached, craving affection.

items.title: Section: The Diligence-Progression Cluster Opens — Excessive Sleep and the Five Marks of Proper Rest

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，嬾惰懈怠，耽睡眠樂、臥樂、倚樂，非時非量，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。無違犯者，若遭疾病；若無氣力；行路疲極，若為斷彼生起樂欲；廣說一切如前應知。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, out of laziness and indolence, indulge the pleasure of sleep, of lying flat, or of reclining against a support, at the wrong time or beyond proper measure — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. ... There is no violation for one who is genuinely ill; who lacks the physical strength to continue; who is exhausted from a long journey; or who genuinely wishes to eliminate this pattern and works diligently towards doing so — all such cases, as described in fuller detail earlier, are without violation.

items.title: Section: Wasting the Day in Idle Worldly Talk — Diligence-Progression Closes

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，懷愛染心，談說世事，虛度時日，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若由忘念，虛度時日，是名有犯，有所違越，非染違犯。無違犯者，見他談說，護彼意故，安住正念須臾而聽；若事希奇；或暫問他，或答他問，無所違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, gripped by attached delight in it, engage in idle worldly conversation and let the day slip meaninglessly away — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. If the wasted time arises instead merely from a lapse of mindfulness, this too is a violation and a transgression, but it is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation for one who, seeing others already engaged in such talk, and wishing to be considerate of their feelings, remains present a brief while, maintaining mindfulness throughout while listening; nor for briefly discussing a matter that happens to be genuinely unusual or noteworthy; nor for briefly asking or answering a question others raise about worldly affairs.

items.title: Section: Refusing, Out of Pride, to Seek Meditation Instruction from a Qualified Teacher

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，為令心住，欲定其心，心懷嫌恨，憍慢所持，不詣師所求請教授，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。嬾惰懈怠而不請者，非染違犯。無違犯者，若遇疾病；若無氣力；若知其師顛倒教授；若自多聞，自有智力能令心定；若先已得所應教授；而不請者，無所違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, wishing to settle and concentrate the mind, are nonetheless gripped by resentment or held fast by arrogance, and so refuse to approach a qualified teacher and formally request instruction — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. Failing to request instruction merely out of laziness or indolence is a non-tainted violation. ... There is no violation for one who is genuinely ill; who lacks the physical strength; who knows the available teacher's instruction is actually mistaken; who already possesses sufficient learning and wisdom of their own to settle the mind unaided; or who has already received the necessary instruction previously.

items.title: Section: Tolerating the Five Hindrances Rather Than Releasing Them

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，起貪欲蓋，忍受不捨，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。無違犯者，若為斷彼生起樂欲，發勤精進，煩惱猛利蔽抑心故，時時現行。如貪欲蓋，如是瞋恚、惛沈睡眠、掉舉惡作，及與疑蓋，當知亦爾。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts in whom the hindrance of sensual craving arises, and who tolerate and retain it rather than releasing it, commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. ... There is no violation for one who genuinely wishes to eliminate it and applies diligent effort towards doing so, even where the affliction is so intense that it still overpowers and obscures the mind and recurs from time to time. Exactly as with the hindrance of sensual craving, so too should the hindrances of ill will; of torpor and drowsiness; of restlessness and worry; and of doubt each be understood.

items.title: Section: The Subtler Danger of Craving Meditative Absorption Itself — Meditation-Progression Closes

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，貪味靜慮，於味靜慮見為功德，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。無違犯者，若為斷彼生起樂欲，廣說如前。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who develop a craving attachment to the flavour of meditative absorption, and regard that very attachment as a genuine spiritual accomplishment, commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. ... There is no violation for one who genuinely wishes to eliminate this attachment and applies diligent effort towards doing so, as described in fuller detail earlier.

items.title: Section: The Wisdom-Progression Cluster Opens — Denigrating the Śrāvaka Teachings

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，起如是見，立如是論：菩薩不應聽聲聞乘相應法教，不應受持，不應修學，菩薩何用於聲聞乘相應法教聽聞、受持、精勤修學？是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。何以故？菩薩尚於外道書論精勤研究，況於佛語。無違犯者，為令一向習小法者捨彼欲故，作如是說。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who form and propound the view that bodhisattvas need not listen to, uphold, or study the teachings associated with the śrāvaka vehicle — reasoning that a bodhisattva has no use for listening to, upholding, and diligently studying the śrāvaka vehicle's teachings — commit a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. Why is this so? A bodhisattva diligently researches even non-Buddhist treatises — how much more so the Buddha's own word! ... There is no violation when a bodhisattva says such things specifically to help someone fixed exclusively on the lesser vehicle let go of that narrow aspiration.

items.title: Section: Neglecting the Bodhisattva Canon Entirely for the Śrāvaka Canon

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，於菩薩藏未精研究，於菩薩藏一切棄捨，於聲聞藏一向修學，是名有犯，有所違越，非染違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who have never diligently studied the bodhisattva canon, who abandon it entirely, and who devote themselves exclusively to studying the śrāvaka canon instead — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, but it is a non-tainted violation.

items.title: Section: Studying Non-Buddhist Treatises While Neglecting the Buddha's Own Word

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，現有佛教，於佛教中未精研究，於異道論及諸外論精勤修學，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。無違犯者，若上聰敏；若能速受；若經久時能不忘失；若於其義能思能達；若於佛教如理觀察成就俱行無動覺者，於日日中，常以二分修學佛語，一分學外；則無違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts who, while the Buddha's teaching genuinely still exists in the world, have never diligently studied it, yet diligently pursue non-Buddhist and rival treatises instead — this constitutes a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation. ... There is no violation for one who is exceptionally intelligent; who can grasp material with unusual speed; who, once learned, does not forget it even after long stretches of time; who is able to reflect on and thoroughly penetrate its meaning; and who, through correct contemplation of the Buddha's teaching, has attained an unshakeable realisation that accompanies every activity — such a bodhisattva may, each day, devote two parts of their time to studying the Buddha's word and one part to non-Buddhist study, without any violation.

blocks.text: Precepts against holding grudges, laziness, and neglect of study.
Refusing "a sincere and proper apology" out of lingering resentment is tainted. Master Cháng Bǎi notes a variant translation.

"Holding anger fast and nursing it": tainted. Master Cháng Bǎi: "even our own teeth bite our tongue; how could there be no friction between people?" And: "if one's breath stopped, which would come first, tomorrow or the next moment?"
Governing a following "with attached craving to be served" is an offence.

Indulging sleep "at the wrong time or beyond measure" (Master Cháng Bǎi: six to eight hours is enough). Wasting the day in worldly talk "with attached delight": tainted; from lapse of mindfulness, untainted.

Refusing out of pride to ask a qualified teacher how to settle the mind. Tolerating the hindrances rather than releasing them (no offence for one who is trying). "Craving the flavour of absorption and regarding that attachment as an accomplishment." Master Cháng Bǎi quotes Venerable Miào Jìng: "a hundred people practise, and all hundred will savour absorption."

Saying bodhisattvas need not study the śrāvaka teachings is an offence (Master Cháng Bǎi: know oneself and the other). So is abandoning the bodhisattva canon for the śrāvaka canon alone. And, while the Buddha's teaching is still available, studying outside treatises instead: one should spend "two parts on the Buddha's word and one part on outside learning".

quiz.q: When the offender sincerely apologises, refusing out of resentment and a wish to hurt them — how is this judged?
quiz.why: Refusing a proper apology out of resentment "is a violation, a transgression, and it is a tainted violation." Master Cháng Bǎi: if the apology is improper or not on an equal footing, declining it is no violation.

quiz.q: On harbouring grudges, what image does Master Cháng Bǎi use to encourage letting go?
options: even our own teeth bite our tongue — how could people never clash?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: think — even our own teeth bite our tongue; how could there be no friction at all between people? And: if one's breath stopped, which would come first — tomorrow or the next moment?

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain sleeping "beyond measure"?
options: six to eight hours suffice, but one sleeps ten or twelve
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: six to eight hours of sleep should be enough; sleeping ten or twelve hours is "beyond measure." In the middle watch one may rest six hours.

quiz.q: If one wastes the day in worldly talk merely through a lapse of mindfulness, how does the treatise judge it?
quiz.why: With attached delight it is tainted; "if the wasted time arises instead merely from a lapse of mindfulness," it is an untainted violation. Venerable Miào Jìng: he just forgot mindfulness for a moment.

quiz.q: Tolerating the hindrance of sensual craving is a tainted violation. When is there no violation?
options: wishing to eliminate it and striving diligently, yet the intense affliction still breaks through from time to time
if it lasts less than a day
quiz.why: "There is no violation for one who genuinely wishes to eliminate it and applies diligent effort." Master Cháng Bǎi: not applying the antidote is a tainted violation; if one does apply it but the innate hindrance is too strong, it is no violation. Venerable Miào Jìng: if you resolve to counter it, it is not a violation — but you can't say you have no fault.

quiz.q: "Craving the flavour of meditative absorption and regarding it as virtue" is a tainted violation. How do the two lectures describe the danger?
options: Cháng Bǎi quotes Miào Jìng: "of a hundred who practice, all hundred will savour absorption," stressing right view first; Miào Jìng's own lecture names four afflictions in savouring: craving, views, pride, ignorance
both: savouring is the noble path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi quotes Miào Jìng: "a hundred people practice, and all hundred will savour absorption," and stresses having the wisdom of the noble path and right view first. Miào Jìng's own lecture names four afflictions present: craving, views, pride, and ignorance. (The "hundred people" line is Cháng Bǎi's report; it is not in Miào Jìng's transcript for this fascicle.)

quiz.q: For an exceptionally gifted bodhisattva, studying outside treatises is no violation if the day is divided how?
options: every day, two parts studying the Buddha's word, one part outside works
quiz.why: "Every day, they constantly devote two parts to studying the Buddha's word and one part to outside learning." Master Cháng Bǎi: two-thirds of each day for the Buddha's teaching, one-third for outside theories.
